To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) early isolation rearing disrupts prepulse inhibition of startle (PPI) in adult male rats, (b) PPI deficits in isolation reared rats are associated with altered auditory-evoked local-field-potentials in the medial prefront cortical region, and (c) PPI and gene expression levels are correlated in the mPfC and nucleus accumben (NAC) of isolation reared rats.

the early-life experience of isolation rearing (IR) disrupts prepulse inhibition (a schizophrenia-related phenotype) in adult rats and that IR alters expression of several genes in the medial prefrontic cortex (mPfc) that regulate PPI.
the effects of early-life experience (isolation) on PPI in adult male BUF rats are moderated by gene expression levels in specific forebrain areas (mPFC and NAc).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of early-life experience (social isolation rearing) on the development of behavioral and neurophysiologic markers of schizophrenia (SZ).
the development of the prefrontal cortex in the male rat.
understanding the role of the environment on the brain and behavior in relation to the etiology of schizophrenia.

the effects of early life experience on gene expression in specific brain regions can be correlated with behavioral and neurophysiologic outcomes in adulthood.
